newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nuevo Leon state in finance crisis-report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nuevo Leon state in finance crisis-report.

text.p: The public finances of the powerful northern state of Nuevo Leon are in deep crisis because of a sharp 13.5 percent drop in federal contributions, the newspaper El Norte reported Thursday, quoting a top local government official.
"The state finances are on the verge of collapse for that reason and this could become a crisis in less than 45 days," the state Secretary of Finance Xavier Doria Gonzalez was quoted as saying.
"If the federal government doesn't take measures before October 30, we'll collapse. We won't make it to the end of the year."
Finance Ministry data released on Wednesday showed that Mexico's states received 35.337 billion pesos in public financing in the first half of 1996, down 1.5 percent from the same period last year.
However, Nuevo Leon, which includes Mexico's second largest city Monterrey, was hardest hit, with its income from federal coffers falling 13.5 percent, to 1.58 billion pesos.
